en: The Śrī Rāma Kavaca from within the illustrious Ānanda Rāmāyaṇa.
Oṃ, salutations to you, Śrī Rāma.
Agastya said:
[I see] one whose arms reach his knees, whose eyes are as broad as lotus petals, whose birth is pure, and whose face has the radiance of a smile of refined essence.
I meditate upon Rāma, who is dark-complexioned, who holds a bow and arrows, whose form is noble, who is accompanied by Sītā, and who is supremely beautiful. || 1 ||
Listen, O Sūtikṣṇa, best of sages; I shall tell you everything—the meritorious armor (kavaca) of Śrī Rāma, which grants all desires.
Rāmacandra shines forth here, both within and without, characterized solely by non-dual bliss, consciousness, and pure being, and possessing an exceedingly sharp brilliance.
Therefore, seekers of knowledge always delight in the Self which is consciousness and bliss;
thus, this state of Rāma is designated as the Supreme Brahman. || 4 ||
One who chants the name "Jayarāma" and does not disparage it, being liberated from all sins, goes to the supreme abode of Viṣṇu. || 5 ||
"Śrī Rāma"—know this to be the supreme mantra, that very same thing is the highest state;
know that alone to be the savior (tāraka) which removes the fear of birth and death.
Uttering "Śrī Rāma," one undoubtedly attains the state of Brahman.
Oṃ. Of this Śrī Rāmakavaca, Agastya is the seer (ṛṣi),
Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chanda),
and the deity (devatā) is Śrī Rāmacandra accompanied by Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa.
The application (viniyoga) is for the purpose of attaining the grace of Śrī Rāmacandra through recitation.
Now I shall proclaim the meditation that bestows all desired fruits:
[He who is] resembling a dark blue cloud, clothed in garments the color of lightning. (1)
With tender limbs, large eyes, youthful, and exceedingly beautiful,
he was accompanied by Sītā and the son of Sumitrā, wearing a crown of matted locks.
When there was fear of thieves, fear of kings, and likewise fear of enemies, [he saw] that crusher of Dānavas with bow, arrow, and sword in hand.
Having meditated upon the Lord of the Raghus, who was enraged and possessed a luster like the fire of cosmic destruction,
wearing bark garments and a black antelope skin, with his body smeared with ashes.
Adorned with arms that drew the bow with arrows fixed to the very ear,
he [struck] his enemies, Rāvaṇa and the others, in battle with showers of sharp shafts.
The great hero, the fierce one, seated upon Indra’s chariot, was destroying [the enemy],
surrounded by great heroes such as Lakṣmaṇa and others, and by Hanumān and his peers.
Accompanied by Sugrīva and other great heroes, who held mountains and trees raised in their hands,
they moved with speed, uttering fierce *huṃkāras* and loud roars like the sound of thunder.
"O Śrī Rāma, with those roaring and shouting in battle against Rāvaṇa, slay, crush, and destroy my hosts of enemies! || 8 ||
"O Śrī Rāma, destroy the bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, and the like!
Having meditated thus, one should recite the *Rāmakavaca*, which bestows spiritual accomplishment (*siddhi*). || 9 ||
O Sutīkṣṇa, listen; I shall proclaim the auspicious Vajrakavaca.
May Śrī Rāma, born of the Raghu lineage, protect my head in the east.
May the best of the Raghus protect my right side; may the Purifier protect my west; may the Lord of the Raghus protect my north; and may the son of Daśaratha protect my forehead.
May Janārdana, dark as a blade of dūrvā grass, protect my two eyebrows; between them, may Rājendra protect my ears, and the lotus-eyed one protect my eyes. 12.
May the royal sage protect my nose; may the husband of Jānakī protect my throat; may the destroyer of Khara protect the base of my ears; and may the beloved of the Raghus protect my forehead. (13)
May the Lord of Speech protect my tongue; may the best of the Raghus protect the two rows of my teeth;
may Śrī Rāmacandra protect my lips; and may the one higher than the highest protect my face. 14.
May he who is worshipped by the world protect my throat; may the destroyer of Rāvaṇa protect my shoulders;
and may the crusher of Vālin, bearing bow and arrow, protect my arms. 15.
May the destroyer of Rākṣasas protect all the joints of my fingers and my two hands;
may the descendant of Kakutstha protect my chest, and may Hari protect my heart.
May the Lord of the World, the husband of Sītā, protect my breasts;
may the Lord of Lakṣmī protect my waist, and may the Leader of the Raghus protect my navel. (17)
May the son of Kausalya protect my waist; may the destroyer of miserable states protect my back; may Hṛṣīkeśa protect my private parts; and may he of true valor protect my two thighs.
May the wielder of the Śārṅga bow protect my thighs; may he who is dear to Hanumān protect my knees;
may the all-pervading Lord protect my shanks; and may the slayer of Tāṭakā protect my feet. || 19 ||
May Viṣṇu protect all my limbs, and may he who is free from ailment protect all my joints; may Madhusūdana protect my senses and my vital breaths, beginning with prāṇa.
May Śrī Rāmabhadra protect me, as well as the objects of the senses such as sound, and all beings beginning with bipeds that are related to me. 21.
May he who destroys the great pride of the sleeping Agni protect those [limbs] of mine;
may the elder brother of Saumitri protect my speech and the other sense organs.
May he who bestows the kingdom upon Sugrīva protect all the sprouts of hair, as well as those actions performed by speech, mind, intellect, ego, and the vital breaths. 23.
Having quickly burnt away all those various sins committed in other births here, he who shattered the bow of Hara [attains this]. (24)
"May Rāma, who always bears the Śārṅga bow and arrows, protect me from all sides.
Thus ends the armor (kavaca) of Śrī Rāmacandra, which is equal to a thunderbolt. 25.
O best of sages, this divine [teaching], more secret than the secret, is extremely sharp; whoever, being composed, should read it, hear it, or cause others to hear it— || 26 ||
By the grace of Rāmacandra, he goes to the supreme abode, whether he be burdened with great sins, a killer of cows, or even a slayer of a Brahmin. || 27 ||
By reciting the Śrī Rāmacandra Kavaca, one attains purity;
one is liberated from sins such as the killing of a Brahmin—of this there is no doubt. (28)
Thus ends the Śrī Rāma-kavaca within the Manohara-kāṇḍa of the venerable Ānanda-rāmāyaṇa by Vālmīki, which is part of the illustrious Śatakoṭi-rama-carita.
